related_questions.question: What do US citizens need to enter Germany?

text_blocks.snippet: US citizens can travel to Germany for up to 90 days within a 180-day period without a visa for tourism, business, or visiting purposes. They will need a valid US passport that is valid for at least three months beyond their intended stay. For stays longer than 90 days, or for work or study, a residence permit or visa is required.
snippet_highlighted_words: a valid US passport that is valid for at least three months beyond their intended stay

list.title: Valid US Passport:
list.snippet: The passport must be valid for at least three months beyond your intended stay.

list.title: No visa required:
list.snippet: US citizens are exempt from needing a visa for short stays in Germany and the Schengen Area.

list.title: Residence permit or visa:
list.snippet: If you plan to stay longer than 90 days, or if you plan to work or study, you will need to apply for a residence permit or a national visa (also known as a Schengen Visa Type D) before entering Germany.

list.title: Application:
list.snippet: You should apply for the appropriate permit or visa at the local immigration office (Ausländerbehörde) in Germany or at a German embassy or consulate in the US.

list.title: ETIAS:
list.snippet: Starting in 2025, US citizens may need to register for ETIAS before traveling to Germany.

list.title: Previous entry denials:
list.snippet: If you have previously been denied entry to the Schengen Area, you may need a visa even for short stays.

list.title: Proof of onward travel:
list.snippet: While not always required, it's a good idea to have proof of onward or return travel (like a plane ticket).

list.title: Travel insurance:
list.snippet: While not mandatory for short stays, travel insurance is recommended, especially if you have pre-existing medical conditions or are engaging in potentially risky activities.

list.title: Other requirements:
list.snippet: Be sure to check for any other specific requirements or recommendations from the German Missions in the United States.
